name: Autoimmune Interstitial Lung Disease-Arthritis Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Criteria for Autoimmune Interstitial Lung Disease-Arthritis Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of inflammatory arthritis involving small or large joints
Radiologically or histologically confirmed interstitial lung disease
Detection of circulating autoimmune antibodies such as ANA, RF, or anti-CCP
Exclusion of other known causes of ILD and arthritis including infection and drug-induced etiologies
Presence of systemic symptoms such as morning stiffness, Raynaud phenomenon, or sicca symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of inflammatory arthritis and confirmed interstitial lung disease with exclusion of other causes; supportive autoimmune serology and systemic features increase diagnostic confidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: No universally accepted formal diagnostic criteria exist; diagnosis is clinical and multidisciplinary.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fibrosing interstitial lung disease with restrictive ventilatory defect
Positive rheumatoid factor or anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies

common.symptomName: Morning joint stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes
searchTerms: stiff joints in morning over 30 minutes
persistent dryness of eyes and mouth
mild anemia due to chronic illness
low red blood cells from long-term disease
high blood pressure in lungs from lung disease
pulmonary hypertension caused by lung scarring

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
Positive rheumatoid factor (RF) and/or anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies
Antinuclear antibody (ANA) positivity in some cases
imaging: High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) showing ground-glass opacities, reticulation, and honeycombing consistent with fibrosing interstitial lung disease
Chest X-ray may show bilateral interstitial infiltrates
other: Pulmonary function tests demonstrating restrictive pattern with reduced diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO)
Bronchoalveolar lavage showing lymphocytic predominance in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of arthritis or autoimmune serology
Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern on HRCT without systemic features

redFlags: Signs of acute exacerbation of interstitial lung disease
references: Fischer A, et al. Interstitial lung disease in autoimmune diseases. Lancet Respir Med. 2020.
Cottin V, et al. Autoimmune interstitial lung disease: clinical features and management. Eur Respir J. 2019.
Orphanet: Autoimmune interstitial lung disease-arthritis syndrome. ORPHA:444092.
